deviations.item: The smoke test uses 64 synthetic items, 8 input dimensions, a compact network, and 8-entry codebooks rather than the frozen production dataset and full 3000-epoch schedule.
deviations.reason: A bounded smoke test is intended to prove the altered preprocessing, finite forward/backward with gradients reaching trainable RQ-VAE parameters, and valid unique SID export without executing a full production training run. Production hyperparameters and schedule in train_rqvae.py remain frozen.

assumptions: The baseline embedding array row order is the item-ID order, and unique target IDs in the existing training parquet define the train-item population for covariance estimation.

The provided train.parquet target IDs represent the existing frozen training split; validation/test items should be transformed with the same train-fitted mean and matrix, as the existing exporter transforms all embedding rows uniformly.
The specified floor 0.01*mean(s) is applied to the eigenvalues of the shrinkage covariance, with rho=0.1 and population covariance denominator N, exactly as stated.

smoke.result: PASS: loss=0.315373, finite loss and finite nonzero gradients on trainable model parameters; transformed output finite; token shape (64, 3); exported extended SID shape (64, 4), all 64 unique.

notes: Copied the frozen baseline TIGER_RQ-VAE train script and model package into the standalone candidate tree. The only production-script behavior change is a single train-ID-only shrinkage covariance/eigendecomposition, application of the frozen transform to every item before RQ-VAE training/evaluation/export, persistence of the fitted mean/matrix, and routing candidate outputs/logs into this owned tree. No model, loss, optimizer, schedule, seeds, split, or exporter logic was changed.
